name: novgraph
description: Novayagraph workflows over this codebase's knowledge graph: review the current change for missing edits, brief a task, trace impact, debug, record why, onboard, summarise the codebase, and show this session's token savings.
argument_hint: review | brief <task> | impact <target> | debug <symptom> | record [commit] | onboard [area] | summary | savings [days]
body:
# {invoke}

The request: {request}

Run the workflow named by its first word, applied to the rest. No request:
list the eight below and stop. `token savings` means `savings`. A first word
that is not one of them: treat the whole request as a task and run `brief`.

| Workflow | For |
| --- | --- |
| `review [base]` | the current change: missing edits, constraints at risk |
| `brief <task>` | before starting: files, reasoning to keep, blast radius, plan |
| `impact <file or symbol>` | what breaks if this changes, most certain first |
| `debug <symptom>` | likely causes, ranked, each with evidence and a check |
| `record [commit]` | write the reasoning behind a commit back to the graph |
| `onboard [area]` | a guided tour of the codebase or one part of it |
| `summary` | the whole codebase at its latest indexed commit, and how current that is |
| `savings [days]` | what Novayagraph saved this session, query by query |

## How to call Novayagraph

Use the Novayagraph MCP tools when this session has them (`novgraph_why`,
`novgraph_impact`, ...); otherwise the shell: `novgraph why <path>`,
`novgraph impact <path>`, `novgraph ask "<task>"`, `novgraph record-why "<why>"
--intent "..." --reasoning "..." --commit <sha>`. Before every call, write one
line naming the real target:

    Novayagraph thinking: tracing what depends on gateway/runner.py

The graph describes the last indexed commit. Code written since, and
uncommitted work, is not in it: read those files directly. When the graph and
the working tree disagree, the working tree is right about what the code says
and the graph is right about why. If a call fails (401, not indexed), say so,
suggest `novgraph doctor`, and stop -- never answer from guesses.

## review [base]

Check the current change for what it is missing. Report; do not edit.

1. The change set: `git status --porcelain` plus `git diff --name-only HEAD`.
   With a base, `git diff --name-only <base>...HEAD`. Nothing uncommitted and
   no base: the last commit, `git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD`. Skip lock
   files, generated and vendored files.
2. For each changed file (the ten most substantial, if more): `impact`.
3. **Missing edits.** Every direct dependent and every file that historically
   changes with it, that is NOT in the change set. Read the diff and the
   dependent to decide whether it really needs a change; list only those that
   plausibly do, each with its evidence.
4. **Constraints at risk.** `why` with precision `precise` on the files the
   graph marks load-bearing. Compare each recorded constraint with the diff.
5. Report:

       Novayagraph review -- <n> files changed
       Likely missing edits
         <path> -- <evidence: imports X / changed with X in 7 of 9 commits>
       Constraints at risk
         <path> -- <constraint> (#<serial>) -- <what in the diff touches it>
       Covered
         <dependents that the change already handles>
       Verdict: <ready | check the items above>

   Files new since the last index have no graph entry: say which, and review
   them from the diff alone.

## brief <task>

Prepare for a task before touching code. End with a plan, not an edit --
unless the user asked you to go ahead and implement.

1. `ask` with the task in your own words.
2. `search` for the concepts the task names, to find the files.
3. For the three to five files that will change: `why` (precision
   `precise`) and `connections`.
4. `impact` on the file most likely to be edited.
5. Report:

       Novayagraph brief -- <task>
       Files to change    <path> -- <its role in this task>
       Keep               <recorded constraint> (#<serial>) -- <source file>
       Also touches       <co-change or dependent that must move with it>
       Risks              <what could break, most certain first>
       Plan               1. ... 2. ... 3. ...

## impact <file or symbol>

What breaks if the target changes. No target: every file in the current
uncommitted change.

1. `impact` on the target.
2. `connections` on it, for historical co-change.
3. `why` with precision `precise`, for constraints the change must keep.
4. Report a checklist, most certain first:

       Novayagraph impact -- <target>
       Will break       <callers and importers, with the symbol they use>
       Moves with it    <co-change partners, with how often>
       Tests            <tests that exercise it, if the graph or a search shows any>
       Keep             <recorded constraints> (#<serial>)

   If the graph says its history is too shallow to judge co-change, repeat
   that rather than implying confidence.

## debug <symptom>

Find the likely cause. Diagnose first; change code only when the user asks.

1. `recent` with limit 15: the changes and their recorded intent.
2. `search` for the symptom's terms: the error text, the feature, the symbol.
3. On the two or three most suspicious files: `why` for their latest
   entries and `connections` for what moved with them.
4. Read the suspect code in the working tree.
5. Report up to three hypotheses, most likely first:

       Novayagraph debug -- <symptom>
       1. <cause> -- evidence: <commit #serial / file / recorded intent>
          Check: <one concrete command, test or read that confirms or rules it out>

   Say plainly when the graph holds nothing relevant, and fall back to
   reading code rather than inventing a history.

## record [commit]

Write the reasoning behind a commit back to the graph. This is how its memory
grows, so it has to be true.

1. The commit: the argument, or `HEAD`. Read `git show --stat` and the diff.
   Use the full SHA. Only a real commit on the indexed branch.
2. `recent`: if this commit already has recorded reasoning, show it and stop.
3. From the diff, the commit message and this session, write:
   - **why** -- one line on what the change is really about
   - **intent** -- the goal being pursued
   - **reasoning** -- why this approach, what was traded away, and any
     constraint discovered. Never a restatement of the diff.
   If the reasoning is not known from this session, ask the user one question
   rather than inventing it.
4. `record_why` with why, intent, reasoning and commit.
5. Report:

       Novayagraph record -- <short sha> <commit subject>
       Recorded   #<serial it returned> -- <why>
       Found by   `novgraph why <a file it touched>`, in any later session

## onboard [area]

A tour for someone new -- the whole codebase, or one area of it.

1. `summary`, then `overview`.
2. `recent` with limit 8, for the current direction.
3. With an area: `search` for it, then `why` and `connections` on its two
   or three central files.
4. Report:

       Novayagraph onboard -- <codebase or area>
       What it is         <two or three sentences>
       How it fits        <subsystems and how they depend on each other>
       Load-bearing       <files to change carefully, and why>
       Recent direction   <what the last changes were for>
       Read first         <five files, one line each on why>
       Next               {invoke} brief <a first task that fits>

## summary

The whole codebase as of its latest indexed commit, and whether that commit is
the latest one.

1. `summary`: its first line names the commit it describes.
2. `overview`, then `recent` with limit 5.
3. `git rev-parse HEAD`. If it differs from the summary's commit,
   `git rev-list --count <summary commit>..HEAD` says how far behind the graph
   is; if the summary's commit is not in the local history, say so.
4. Report:

       Novayagraph summary -- <codebase> at <short sha> (<latest | N commits behind your HEAD>)
       What it is         <two or three sentences, from the summary>
       How it is built    <subsystems, and the load-bearing files>
       Recent direction   <what the last changes were for>

   Behind: say the graph re-indexes within minutes of each push, and that
   files changed since are best read directly until it does.

## savings [days]

What Novayagraph saved in this agent session. The numbers are measured by the
server; report them, never re-estimate them.

1. `savings`, with `days` if the user named a period.
2. Report what it returned, in this shape:

       Novayagraph savings -- <agent>, this session
       <each query: what was asked, tokens returned, tokens its cited files hold, saved>
       This session       <total saved, and how much less than reading>
       Earlier sessions   <this agent's recent sessions, if any>

   A saving compares each answer with reading the files it cites -- a size
   comparison, not billing. A query without a measurable baseline is shown as
   such, never as zero.
